title.narrative: IOM: Peace Agreement´s transitional justice system

description.narrative: Detta är ett stöd till ett IOM-program med titeln "Fredsavtalets system för övergångsrättvisa”. Syftet är att stödja det system för övergångsrättvisa (SIVJRNR, förkortning på spanska) som upprättades i samband med fredsavtalet som ingicks mellan den colombianska regeringen och FARC-gerillan, samt att främja offrens och det civila samhällets deltagande i detta system. Programmet fungerar som en fond som stöder projekt med syftet att: (i) Stärka institutionerna och mekanismerna för övergångsrättvisa inom SIVJRNR; (ii) Främja det civila samhällets och offrens deltagande i SIVJRNR; och (iii) Stödja förtroendeskapande åtgärder mellan regeringen, FARC och det civila samhället.

This is a support to a specific-purpose programme and fund managed by IOM, titled “Programme for the support of the Peace Agreement’s Transitional Justice System”. The purpose is to support the Transitional Justice System (SIVJRNR for its acronym in Spanish) created through the Peace Agreement between the Colombian government and the FARC guerrilla, as well as to promote the participation of victims and civil society within that system. The Programme acts as a fund supporting projects oriented towards: (i) Strengthening the transitional justice institutions and mechanisms within the SIVJRNR; (ii) Promoting the participation of civil society and victims in the SIVJRNR; and (iii) Supporting trust-building measures between the Government, the FARC, and civil society.

Outcome: Contribute to the implementation of the Transitional Justice system (SIVJRNR) and promote the participation of victims and civil society in the system.
Output 1:Entities and mechanisms of the SIVJRNR have technical and financial capacity to perform their duties.
Output 2: Civil society and victims have capacity and information for their participation in the SIVJRNR
Output 3: The Government and Civil Society have capacities for the formulation and development of trust building actions within the implementation of the Peace Agreement.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
The fund, that was expected to be active until December 2022, was amended to function additional 14 months (until April 2024) to strengthen the JEPs capacities to undertake all activities related to placing the restorative system and establishing effective mechanisms to back the investigation tasks defined for new Macrocases 8, 9 and 10. With regards to the work with the UBPD, the fund approved three additional projects to support activities related to strengthening the institutional capacities to advance the Huila Missing Persons Search Plan, and adding research personnel and equipment to capture and systematise information on the former FARC South Division and paramilitary groups graves.
By December 31st, 2022, 27 projects had been supported by the Program aiming at strengthening the transitional justice system created by the Peace Agreement. Out of these projects, eight were directly implemented by IOM in coordination with strategic partners -Special Jurisdiction for Peace (SJP), Truth Commission, Unit for the Search of Missing Persons and victims organizations-, while seventeen initiatives are carried out through grants with victims organizations, former Farc members and civil society organizations. All supported projects have nearly covered 22 departments and 114 municipalities with an investment that reaches up to SEK 24 000 000.
Milestones related to the results of the Program are:
Missing Persons Search Unit (UBPD for its acronym in Spanish)
- The project developed a strategy between the FARC Search Commission and the UBPD that provided information on 402 new cases with complementary information to identify missing persons within the armed conflict dynamics. Moreover, 101 former FARC members finalised their training in tailored methodologies to collect, analyse and systematise information to localise missing persons.
- To consolidate the operation of the national and regional search plans, in 2022 the project continued supporting implementation of the North Caquetá regional plan. Significant progress was made in this front to operationalise and systematise a working model that engages institutional and Civil Society efforts to find missing persons registered in the national victims' system.
Special Jurisdiction for Peace (JEP for its acronym in Spanish)
- Technical assistance provided by the project permitted the conceptualisation of victims categories that permitted a deeper analysis and understanding of the way paramilitary and guerrilla fronts operated in different territories and the differentiated impacts the conflict had over the victims' processes and organisations. Moreover the project pushed forward the update of 7 strategic documents that elaborate on former FARC structures that will serve as proof to the Special Jurisdiction for Peace to investigate the existing macrocases. It is worth mentioning that these documents are likely to contribute to opening three new macrocases during 2022 (these cases will further elaborate on a) the impacts of the armed conflict on ethnic communities; b) paramilitary structures and their role in advancing violence in Colombia; and c) sexual violence).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
